message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Compute Engine** instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

| Method | What you’ll run | Where it lives |
|--------|-----------------|----------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Your local terminal (or Cloud Shell) |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/...` | Any HTTP client (curl, Postman, your own script) |

> ⚠️ **Important** – Google Cloud does *not* use “EC2”; that’s Amazon Web Services. In GCP the equivalent service is **Compute Engine**.

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI

```bash
# 1. Pick a name, zone, and machine type
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # change to your preferred zone
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-highmem-8"   # 8 vCPU, 52 GiB RAM – adjust as needed

# 2. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=50GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
    --boot-disk-device-name="$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: run a script at boot
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | The GCP zone where the VM will live. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM profile. Choose one that supports GPUs (e.g., `n1-highmem-8`, `n1-standard-16`). |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `type=nvidia-tesla-a6000` is the RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu project. |
| `--boot-disk-*` | Size/type of the root disk. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: a shell script that runs on first boot (useful for installing drivers, CUDA, etc.). |

> **Tip:** If you’re running this from Cloud Shell, you already have the `gcloud` SDK installed and authenticated.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the API directly (e.g., from a custom deployment tool), here’s the minimal JSON payload you’d POST to the Compute Engine endpoint:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-highmem-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "labels": { "env": "demo" },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-8"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to POST it

```bash
PROJECT_ID="my-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> Replace `@instance.json` with the path to a file containing the JSON above, or pipe the JSON directly.

---

## 🔧  After Creation

Once the instance is up, you’ll still need to:

1. **Install NVIDIA drivers** (the GPU driver isn’t pre‑installed on Ubuntu images).
2. **Install CUDA / cuDNN** if you plan to run GPU workloads.
3. **Open firewall ports** (e.g., SSH `22`, custom app ports).

A simple startup script (`startup.sh`) that does the driver installation could look like:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install prerequisites
apt-get install -y build-essential dkms linux-headers-$(uname -r)

# Add NVIDIA package repo
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin
mv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600
add-apt-repository "deb http://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/ /"

# Install the driver (replace 525 with the latest supported version)
apt-get update
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-525

# Reboot to activate the driver
reboot
```

> **Note:** The exact driver version (`525` in the example) should match the CUDA toolkit you intend to install later.

---

## 📌 Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Enable Compute Engine API in your project. |
| ✅ | Ensure you have the right IAM permissions (`roles/compute.admin` or similar). |
| ✅ | Verify the zone supports the RTX A6000 (check [GPU availability](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus)). |
| ✅ | Set up billing for the project. |
| ✅ | Optionally, add a firewall rule to allow SSH (`22`) and any other ports you need. |

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
